OK, let me seriously think about the game design. L-shaped path, 5 dots, clicking a dot in the horizontal arm spawns a ball + ring, clicking a dot in the vertical arm does nothing, arrow keys do nothing, ACTION7 does nothing.
Wait... what if the arrow keys move the ball, but the ball only exists in the horizontal arm, and moves along the arm? I tried RIGHT from (18,18) — no change. But what if the ball needs to "launch" first: e.g. press an arrow key to set direction, then ACTION7 to launch? I pressed LEFT twice then... no, I never did ACTION7 after the arrow keys. Actually, in the current state (ball@(18,24), ring@(18,11)), let me try: LEFT, then ACTION7.
Or, the ring might be a "target" and the game might be: move the ball onto the ring to collect the dot? The ball is at 24, the ring is at 11. Move the ball left 3 blocks to 11. If the arrow keys move the ball block by block, then LEFT×3 should put the ball on the ring. Let me try LEFT×3 and check.
Actually wait — earlier I pressed RIGHT once from ball@(18,18) and the board didn't change (only the bar). If the ball moved block by block, it should have moved to (18,24) (where there's a dot). The diff was empty. So the arrow keys don't move the ball block by block.
Hmm, what if the arrow keys move the ball continuously until it hits a wall, and the ball is at (18,18)... RIGHT should move it to (18,47) (the last block). No change. So the arrow keys really do nothing to the ball.
Let me reconsider. What if the ball isn't a player piece but a "preview" of where the ball will be placed, and the actual game is: click a dot to select it, and the ring shows the "pair partner"? Like a matching game: dots pair up: (17,29)? No, there's no dot at 29.
Or maybe the ring shows where the ball will go if you click the same dot again? Let me test: click (18,24) again (the ball is already at 24). If the ball moves to 11 (the ring's position), then the ring = next position.
